candidates: When chaining component name fallbacks in the vue3-vite docgen plugins (vue-docgen.ts and vue-component-meta.ts), use the nullish coalescing operator (`??`) consistently — not logical OR (`||`) — e.g. `component.name ?? component.__name`. `??` is semantically more precise for name-type properties (only skips `null`/`undefined`, not empty strings like `''`) and keeps both plugin files in sync; mixing operators between the two files is a flag for inconsistency.

When merging a runtime-inferred component `displayName` with statically-extracted docgen metadata in the vue3-vite plugins, always pass the runtime-derived defaults as the *first* argument to `Object.assign` and the `meta` object as the *second* (overriding) argument — e.g. `Object.assign({ displayName: runtimeName }, meta)` — so that any `displayName` already present in the static analysis result takes precedence over the runtime fallback.

Any code in the vue3-vite docgen plugins that reads Vue's internal `__name` property (added by the SFC compiler for `<script setup>` components) should include an inline comment noting that `__name` is an undocumented implementation detail, not a public API, that may be absent in production builds or change across Vue/compiler versions. Always pair it with a fallback to the public `name` option or the statically-extracted `displayName` so the feature degrades gracefully.
